# Independent preparation review of the canonical label adapter

Status: local, non-normative technical review by `/root/isometry_docs`.
I fully read the frozen generator, adapted-capture driver, README, input map,
retained unexecuted draft, reused three capture scripts and current native API
client source. I also checked the current request decoder, positional port
rules and conditional Fourier theorems. No candidate was imported, generated
or executed; no CLI/native call or build was performed.

No blocking defect was found for this fixed four-packet experiment. At widths
1–3 the generator replaces only the existing entry definition, corresponding
meaning and proof rows. It appends distinct definition/meaning/proof indices
for a positional identity prefix, positional identity post-route and composed
enter sequence, plus a new canonical encoding. Original encoding rows remain
unchanged. Each table is indexed separately; equal historical indices are
not assumed by the algorithm.

The resulting root keeps the original Fourier body at child position 1 and
all original suffix children in order. The prefix enters the original input
interface; the post-route maps the old output interface to the canonical one.
Both maps use `owners=[0]` and `axes=0..n-1` as positions. They do not sort or
reinterpret the old axis labels. In particular, the output labels `[1,0]` and
`[2,1,0]`, the actual reversal, phase/control/count data and complete nonroot
rows remain in the original body and suffix. The fixed code checks complete
sequence endpoints, child cardinalities and proof associations, exact finite
string UTF-8 bytes, whole-table reachability and absence of another incoming
root reference. These are local structural assertions, not a semantic checker.

Width zero retains its sole `Q<Bits<0>>` owner, exact single rewire body,
`owners=[0], axes=[], classical=[]` permutation and unchanged proof. Only the
definition/meaning endpoint labels and sole identity encoding change. No
`Unit`, zero-owner interface, scalar, phase, alternative request constructor
or success-driven fallback is inserted.

The recorder selects eight literal API calls: inspect then the original
independent request at widths 0–3. Maps supply only identities, never executable
argv. Generation and capture use separate exclusive output directories, with
no retry or repair. Capture additionally requires a root-reviewed hash of the
ten generated data members before use. Root must inspect those actual generated
rows and their associations; this preparation review supplies no future map

The reused wrapper still allows only the three fixed hierarchy modes with
